expected_outcomes: Potentially applicable authority, required controls, unknown facts, evidence, and legal-review boundaries are explicit.
required_actions: Classify authority, resolve applicability inputs, compile triggered controls and documents, preserve source dates, and escalate high-risk or uncertain scope.
expected_documents: Applicable notices, inventories, assessments, retention schedules, incident plans, rights processes, and release attestations.
acceptance: Official sources remain canonical, guidance is not promoted to binding law, and jurisdiction-specific review remains visible.
verification: Review authority class, source freshness, applicability facts, triggered controls, unknowns, and counsel escalation.
evidence: Source records, applicability report, document inventory, review receipt, and unresolved legal questions.
failure_conditions: Automated output uses COMPLIANT as a final legal status.
A proposal, trend, translation, or guidance source is silently treated as binding law.
exceptions: Legal templates remain drafts requiring jurisdiction-specific qualified review.
No automated result constitutes legal advice or a global compliance certification.
